gloss: rival warlords; rival heroes; competing powers

definitions.gloss: rival warlords; rival heroes; competing powers
definitions.explanation: Multiple powerful leaders or factions competing for dominance. Originally used for warring feudal lords, now also applied figuratively to businesses, athletes, or other competitors vying for the top position.

examples.japanese: {戦国時代|せんごくじだい}は{群雄|ぐんゆう}{割拠|かっきょ}の{時代|じだい}だった。
examples.english: The Sengoku period was an era of rival warlords vying for power.

examples.japanese: IT{業界|ぎょうかい}は{群雄|ぐんゆう}が{競|きそ}い{合|あ}う{世界|せかい}だ。
examples.english: The IT industry is a world where rival powers compete with one another.

examples.japanese: {群雄|ぐんゆう}の{中|なか}から{一人|ひとり}の{覇者|はしゃ}が{現|あらわ}れた。
examples.english: From among the rival powers, one champion emerged.

notes:
USAGE:
{群雄|ぐんゆう} literally means "a group of heroes" and most commonly appears in the compound {群雄割拠|ぐんゆうかっきょ} (rival warlords each holding their own territory). While historically about feudal warfare, it is now widely used as a metaphor for intense competition in business, sports, and other fields.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {群雄割拠|ぐんゆうかっきょ} (rival powers each occupying their own territory — set expression)
- {群雄|ぐんゆう}が{競|きそ}い{合|あ}う (rival powers compete with each other)
- {群雄|ぐんゆう}の{一人|ひとり} (one of the competing powers)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{覇者|はしゃ} refers to the eventual winner or champion who emerges from the competition. {群雄|ぐんゆう} refers to the multiple competitors collectively, before a single winner is determined.
